body:
**Description**

## ESLint Local Rules
To enforce specific coding practices, custom ESLint rules are defined in `eslint-local-rules.js`. These rules can be used to catch common mistakes or enforce project-specific conventions.

### Example Rule: No Original Prisma Client Inside Transaction
This rule prevents using the original Prisma client inside a transaction, ensuring that the transaction context is used instead.

```javascript
async function main() {
  prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => {
    await prisma.user.findFirst(); // ❌ incorrect, should use `tx`
    await tx.user.findFirst(); // ✅ correct
  });
}
```

Test the rule with:
```bash
cd api/
npx eslint src/ --rule 'local-rules/no-original-prisma-inside-tx: error'

author: digitally557
body:
# Emergency Medical Access Control System

## Overview
This pull request introduces a secure, compliant emergency medical access system that allows designated contacts and healthcare providers to access patient records during emergencies. It ensures full auditability, privacy, and patient control.

---

## Problem Addressed
- Delayed access to medical records in emergencies
- Lack of audit-compliant access trails
- No system for patients to pre-authorize emergency contacts
- Legal risks for healthcare providers

---

## Key Components

### Smart Contract (`health-records.clar`)
- Manages emergency contacts and access logs
- Enforces role-based access and audit trails
- Functions:
  - `add-emergency-contact`
  - `remove-emergency-contact`
  - `emergency-access-record`
  - `toggle-emergency-access-system`
  - `can-emergency-access`, `is-emergency-contact`, etc.

### Frontend
- React-based UI with three tabs:
  - Health Records
  - Emergency Contacts
  - Emergency Access
- Real-time blockchain state sync
- Contract interactions via custom React hooks
- Mobile responsive and WCAG 2.1 AA compliant

---

## Security
- Multi-layer access validation
- Immutable audit logs on blockchain
- Global system toggle for emergency mode
- Input validation and role-based restrictions

---

## Privacy
- Only metadata on-chain
- Records stored encrypted in Gaia
- Complies with HIPAA, 21st Century Cures Act, and state laws

---

## Testing

### Smart Contract
- 8 test cases (functional + security)
- Positive and boundary path coverage

### Frontend
- Integration and workflow testing
- Wallet compatibility
- Cross-browser and mobile responsiveness

---

## Performance

### Blockchain
- Gas-optimized functions
- Efficient read operations
- Batch support for multiple contacts

### Frontend
- Lazy-loaded emergency components
- Caching to reduce contract calls
- Graceful fallback during network issues

---

## Deployment Plan
1. Testnet deployment
2. Third-party smart contract audit
3. Beta testing with healthcare professionals
4. Mainnet deployment with rollback support

---

## Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|-------------|--------|------------|
| Smart contract bugs | Low | High | Audits and test coverage |
| Network congestion | Medium | High | Caching, multiple providers |
| Frontend issues | Low | Medium | Cross-browser testing |
| Legal non-compliance | Medium | Medium | Legal consultation |

---

## Success Metrics

### Technical
- >99.5% access success rate
- <30s response time
- >99.9% system uptime

### User Experience
- >95% contact setup completion
- <2 minutes emergency access flow
- >4.5/5 user satisfaction

### Business Impact
- Healthcare partnerships
- Increased emergency access usage
- Strong patient engagement

---

## Files Changed
- `contracts/health-records.clar`
- `contracts/tests/health-records_test.ts`
- `frontend/src/app/page.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/EmergencyContacts.tsx`
- `frontend/src/components/EmergencyAccess.tsx`
- `frontend/src/hooks/useEmergencyAccess.ts`

---

## Next Steps
- Perform external smart contract audit
- Finalize documentation
- Start beta testing
- Plan provider integration

---

## Status
**Ready for testing and audit.

author: jjjj12212
body:
# 4.6
  - Options
    - New options
      - Big Top Tickets are now randomized
      - Targitzan's Green Relics are now randomized
      - Beans are now randomized
        - Locations that requires the bean item will not be in-logic until both beans are collected.
      - New option to open the front door to Grunty's Industries
      - Tag-Link
        - only applies if you use the D-Pad Instant Transformation. Will not work if you manual transform.
      - You can now randomize boss loading zones
        - Loading zones check for the requirement of the randomized boss to see if you can go through them.
        - Terry loading zone behaviour
          - The loading zone at the top of the mountain is randomized, but the one that leads inside the mountain is not.
          - Both loading zones leading to the nest lead to Terry if you're going through them as solo Banjo.
        - HFP flight pad & Claw Clamber Boots no longer requires Dragon Brothers to shoot at, even if bosses are not randomized.
    - The hints with random entrances have been changed.
      - When hinting something that is in a boss room, the area that leads to the boss room will be revealed, if boss loading zones are randomized.
        - An example: g0goTBC's Mumbo Token is at jjjj12212's Weldar's Mumbo Token at Chuffy's Cabin.
      - For items that are not in boss rooms, if level entrance loading zones are randomized, "Entrance" has been added to the hint to make it more distinguishable from the boss entrance hints.
        - An example: g0goTBC's Big-O Pants is at MiaSchemes' TDL: Scrotty Jiggy at Hailfire Peaks Entrance
    - The existing options have been embellished
      - Game length has been renamed to World Requirements.
      - A couple of option descriptions have been reworded.
      - The options page now uses option groups to make it more organized.
      - The options in the yaml have been reordered to match the option page.
  - Grunty gives more varied messages when you die.
  - Changed the error that happens when you select intended logic and randomized worlds, It now says that you are using intended logic instead of beginner logic.
  - Renamings:
    - WW: Inferno Egg Nest -> WW: The Inferno Egg Nest
    - Pawno's Cheato Page -> Pawno Cheato Page
    - Fake Mumbo Skull Jinjo -> Mingy Jongo Skull Jinjo
  - Logic fixes:
    - Added additional regions for randomized bosses.
    - Many bugs related to indirect conditions have been fixed.
    - SM Cheato Page: in hard tricks, can be gotten by jumping off and on the rock during the spring pad animation, making it reachable without any jump move.
    - IoH Another Digger Tunnel Nests: easy tricks can get them by arriving from wasteland and using beak buster.
    - MT Pool Jinjo: Added Golden Goliath and Stony for intended logic.
    - Fuel Depot Nests: Added the clockwork shot from GGM to glitched logic.
    - Dodgem Dome Jiggy: Fixed some nonsense logic.
    - WW Humba Warp Pad: can be tagged with leg spring on easy tricks.
    - Star Spinner Jiggy: Added Leg Spring and Turbo Trainers as a way to get the jiggy in easy tricks.
    - TDL Train Station access: easy tricks can get them with beak buster.
    - TDL Stomping Plains jiggy: removed shoe smuggling from the logic. It made seeds unbeatable with randomized warp pads.
    - GI Floor 1 Guarded Jiggy: Added Tall Jump or Leg Spring to jump high enough to touch the jiggy.
    - GI Floor 1 to Floor 2: Removed solo Kazooie from the logic because it made seeds unbeatable with randomized warp pads.
    - GI Floor 3 to Floor 2: Added Tall Jump + (Flutter or Air Rat-a-tat Rap) to hard tricks
    - Individual alien kids: check if you can reach JRL to do the UFO jiggy.
    - Icicle Grotto Near Spring Pads Nest: can be gotten by warping there.
    - Dragon Brothers Jiggy: Removed Pack Whack from the advanced logic requirement due to the fact that Biggafoot is pre-hit.
    - Central Cavern jinjo: Fixed a bug where the logic did not check for warp pads when it expected the player to warp to the entrance with Claw Clambers.
    - Sack Race Exit Note: No noeed for glide and Claw Clamber to reach it from inside. Just Claw Clamber Boots is enough.

body:
Previously, the `unit_testing` and `native_sim` platforms would use a 32-bit `time_t` due to the `-m32` cflag.

However, on glibc-based systems (at least), this can be controlled via `-D__USE_TIME_BITS64=1`. 

Using a 64-bit `time_t` is important for historical reasons, to be robust for the future, and also just for compatibility with all other platforms supported by Zephyr, as well as the greater Internet-of-Things at large.

With that, we can move `tests/lib/timespec_util` to `tests/unit/timeutil`, since those tests are now platform-independent.

body:
Allows for defining additional objects in case they are needed, e.g. Traefik middleware for Ingress:

```
additionalObjects:
  - apiVersion: traefik.io/v1alpha1
    kind: Middleware
    metadata:
      name: enforce-https
    spec:
      redirectScheme:
        scheme: https
        permanent: true
```

This does not mess with existing parameters and is entirely on the side. Running `helm template` provides additional object:

```
# Source: vikunja/templates/additional-objects.yaml
apiVersion: traefik.io/v1alpha1
kind: Middleware
metadata:
  name: enforce-https
spec:
  redirectScheme:
    permanent: true
    scheme: https
```

author: danmacdonald
body:
**Fix flaky tx_commitments test by ensuring epoch blocks are confirmed before shutdown**

The `tx_commitments::heavy_test_commitments_3epochs_test` was experiencing intermittent failures due to a race condition introduced by recent changes to block migration and validation. 

**Problem:** The test was shutting down before all blocks were consistently written to the block_index, causing non-deterministic test results.

**Solution:** The test now waits for epoch blocks to be confirmed before initiating shutdown. With `block_migration_depth = 1`, this ensures blocks are properly written to the block_index and persisted during graceful shutdown, eliminating the race condition.

author: mergify[bot]
body:
## Why I'm doing:
A flink-connector task imports multiple tables, restarts leader FE, current checkpoint A fails, and there are 2 states of transactions in CPA: prepare/prepared.

After flink task restart, playback starts from CPA, rollback is performed for transactions in prepare state, and commit is performed for transactions in prepared state. but the commit operation will fail because the callback is not persisted, and the callback is lost after FE restart(beginLoadTaskFromFrontend don't edit log).

There are two solutions:
1 Replace the label, but the topic offset of the prepared transaction is already from x--->y, replacing the label is consumed from y, and the data between x and y will be lost.
2 Playback from A-1, so that if it is a DUPLICATE KEY table, will lead to duplicate data import.

## What I'm doing:

BACKEND_STREAMING does not need to rely on callbacks:
1 beginLoadTaskFromBackend does not do the logCreateStreamLoadJob action and the BACKEND StreamLoadTask is not persisted.
2 StreamLoadMgr does not load BACKEND StreamLoadTask when leader FE is restarted

Fixes #60244

This pull request introduces several enhancements to the school activities management system, including new activity options, improved backend validation for participant signups, and updated frontend features to display participant lists. It also includes corresponding style updates to improve the user interface.

### Backend Enhancements:

* **New Activities Added:** Introduced six new activity options categorized into sports, artistic, and intellectual activities, each with a description, schedule, maximum participants, and initial participants (`src/app.py`).
* **Signup Validation:** Enhanced the `signup_for_activity` function to validate if a student is already signed up and to ensure the maximum participant limit is not exceeded before adding a new participant (`src/app.py`).

### Frontend Updates:

* **Participants List Display:** Added functionality to dynamically display a list of participants for each activity on the frontend. If no participants are signed up, a placeholder message is shown (`src/static/app.js`).

### UI Styling:

* **Participants Section Styles:** Added new CSS styles to format the participants section, including a border, heading styles, and list item formatting for better readability (`src/static/styles.css`).

author: davidme-stripe
body:
[testing a bot]

## Summary
Fixes a flaky test that was crashing with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` on `FutureQueue` due to a race condition in async Promise/Future operations.

## Problem
The test `testNextViewControllerDocumentWarmup()` was failing intermittently in CI with:
- **Crash Type**: EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV) 
- **Location**: FutureQueue (async dispatch queue in Promise/Future implementation)
- **Root Cause**: Race condition where test completion raced with async Promise callbacks

The crash occurred because:
1. `mockMLModelLoader.documentModelsPromise.resolve()` triggered async callbacks
2. `nextViewController()` calls happened immediately after
3. Test expectations could complete before all async operations finished
4. Async operations continued after test teardown, accessing deallocated memory

## Solution
- **Synchronized async operations**: Moved promise resolution before `nextViewController` calls
- **Added async dispatch**: Used `DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter` to ensure promise resolution completes
- **Improved error handling**: Added proper error handling in async block to prevent test hangs  
- **Extended timeout**: Increased from 1 to 2 seconds to account for async operations

## Test plan
- [x] Verified fix addresses the specific crash scenario
- [x] Applied linter formatting automatically
- [x] Maintains existing test behavior and assertions

body: ### Related GitHub Issue Closes: #2992 Closes: #5409 Closes: #4807 ### Description ## Issue The `list_files` tool with `recursive: true` was returning empty results when targeting directories that start with a dot (e.g., `.roo-memory`). This happened because the recursive mode was applying a blanket exclusion pattern `!**/.*//**` that excluded all files inside any hidden directory, even when the user explicitly requested to list that directory. ## Files Changed - `src/services/glob/list-files.ts` ## Solution - **Modified `buildRecursiveArgs()`**: Removed the problematic `!**/.*//**` exclusion pattern for hidden directories in recursive mode - **Enhanced `listFilteredDirectories()`**: Added `isTargetDir` parameter to distinguish between explicitly targeted directories and discovered subdirectories - **Updated `shouldIncludeDirectory()`**: Always include explicitly targeted directories (even if hidden), while still applying ignore rules to subdirectories found during traversal ## Behavior Changes - **Before**: `list_files` with `path: ".roo-memory"` and `recursive: true` → Empty results - **After**: `list_files` with `path: ".roo-memory"` and `recursive: true` → Returns directory contents - **Preserved**: Hidden subdirectories discovered during traversal are still filtered out This maintains consistency with `.gitignore` and `.rooignore` mechanisms while ensuring explicitly targeted directories are always processed. ### Test Procedure - Create a .roo-memory (or .whatever) folder. - Create random files inside the folder - Ask Roo to list the contents of the folder recursively - Before the changes, it did not show results. # Git Commit Report

**Commit Range:** `1c82350ac607575bceb7352abc9ac35c9a836dc6` → `f4a6dd3fd256dc00292213c32271fb4900ea1c0e`

## 📋 Summary
重构运行时架构，实现单例模式管理和混合环境DAG执行支持，提升系统的可扩展性和资源管理效率。

## 🔧 Major Changes

### 1. **运行时架构重构**
- **LocalRuntime & RayRuntime**: 实现单例模式设计
  - 添加线程安全的 `get_instance()` 和 `reset_instance()` 方法
  - 统一资源管理和生命周期控制
  - 支持直接节点级别管理而非DAG级别调度

### 2. **节点管理增强**
- **LocalDAGNode** (原MultiplexerDagNode): 重构本地节点架构
  - 实现输入缓冲区机制，支持 `(channel, data)` 包格式
  - 添加 `put()` 方法接收上游数据
  - 集成 `LocalEmitContext` 支持混合环境通信

- **RayDAGNode** (原RayMultiplexerDagNode): 优化Ray Actor节点
  - 移除不必要的输入缓冲区，利用Ray平台自动队列
  - 简化生命周期管理和连接处理
  - 集成 `RayEmitContext` 支持TCP回传通信

### 3. **通信层重构**
- **EmitContext架构**: 实现混合环境智能通信
  ```
  BaseEmitContext (抽象基类)
  ├── LocalEmitContext (本地节点通信)
  └── RayEmitContext (Ray Actor通信 + TCP)
  ```
- **通信协议**:
  - 本地到本地：直接缓冲区写入
  - 本地到Ray：远程方法调用
  - Ray到本地：TCP数据传输
  - Ray到Ray：直接Actor调用

### 4. **混合DAG执行**
- **MixedDAG**: 新增混合环境DAG执行引擎
  - 自动节点平台识别和分离
  - 智能连接建立（本地缓冲区 vs Ray远程调用 vs TCP）
  - `run()` 方法实现一键启动混合环境执行
  - 完整的状态监控和错误处理

### 5. **运行时管理器**
- **RuntimeManager**: 单例模式运行时管理器
  - 延迟初始化和资源管理
  - 跨平台任务提交统一接口
  - 支持本地和Ray运行时的生命周期管理

### 6. **TCP服务器集成**
- **LocalRuntime**: 内置TCP服务器
  - 监听Ray Actor的数据传输请求
  - 自动路由到对应本地节点的输入缓冲区
  - 多线程处理TCP连接

## 🛠️ Technical Improvements

### 单例模式实现
```python
@classmethod
def get_instance(cls, **kwargs):
    if cls._instance is None:
        with cls._lock:
            if cls._instance is None:
                instance = super().__new__(cls)
                instance.__init__(**kwargs)
                cls._instance = instance
    return cls._instance
```

### 节点注册机制
```python
# 提交到对应运行时
local_handles = local_runtime.submit_nodes(local_nodes)
ray_handles = ray_runtime.submit_nodes(ray_actors, node_names)
```

### 智能通信路由
```python
def _route_and_send(self, target: DownstreamTarget, data: Any):
    if target.node_type == NodeType.LOCAL:
        self._send_to_local(target, data)  # 缓冲区写入
    elif target.node_type == NodeType.RAY_ACTOR:
        self._send_to_ray_actor(target, data)  # 远程调用
```

## 📈 Benefits

1. **架构统一性**: 单例模式确保运行时实例的全局一致性
2. **混合执行能力**: 支持本地和Ray节点的无缝混合部署
3. **通信优化**: 智能路由减少跨平台通信开销
4. **资源管理**: 改进的生命周期控制和错误恢复机制
5. **开发体验**: 简化的API接口和更好的调试支持

## 🔍 Files Modified

**核心运行时**:
- local_runtime.py - 本地运行时单例化和TCP服务器
- ray_runtime.py - Ray运行时重构和节点管理
- runtime_manager.py - 单例模式运行时管理器

**节点架构**:
- local_dag_node.py - 本地节点重构（原multi_dag_node.py）
- ray_dag_node.py - Ray节点重构（原ray_multi_node.py）
- mixed_dag.py - 混合DAG执行引擎

**通信层**:
- emit_context.py - 通信上下文基类
- local_emit_context.py - 本地通信实现
- ray_emit_context.py - Ray通信实现

**配置和测试**:
- engine.py - 引擎集成新架构
- qa_dense_retrieval_mixed.py - 混合环境测试
- config.yaml - 添加平台配置支持

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes

1. **运行时实例化**: 从直接构造函数改为 `get_instance()` 方法
2. **节点提交接口**: 从DAG级别改为节点级别管理
3. **通信协议**: 从简单方法调用改为多路复用缓冲区模式
4. **配置格式**: 操作符配置需要添加 `platform` 字段

## 🎯 Migration Guide

### 运行时使用
```python
# 旧方式
local_runtime = LocalRuntime(max_slots=4)
ray_runtime = RayRuntime()

# 新方式
local_runtime = LocalRuntime.get_instance(max_slots=4)
ray_runtime = RayRuntime.get_instance()
```

### 混合DAG执行
```python
# 新功能
pipeline = Pipeline(name="mixed_pipeline")
# ... 构建pipeline ...
pipeline.submit_mixed(config)  # 自动混合环境执行
```

## 🚀 Next Steps

1. 完善TCP连接池管理和重连机制
2. 添加节点健康检查和自动故障恢复
3. 优化跨平台序列化性能
4. 扩展监控和调试工具
5. 完善单元测试和集成测试覆盖

---
**Impact**: 🔴 High - 重大架构重构  
**Testing**: ⚠️ 需要全面的集成测试  
**Documentation**: 📝 API文档需要更新

author: datacore-sbala
body:
# SSV-24884

## WHAT
* Added `--suppress-result` flag to hide the final summary from stdout — useful for scripted or automated runs.
* Progress bar updates are now limited to once every second instead of on every thread update.
* The progress bar now displays an intermediate deduplication ratio.
* Final summary includes additional details: Space Scanned, Non-Zero Data Allocated, Data Unique, and DeDup Ratio.

## HOW
* `tqdm` is not thread-safe, so frequent updates from multiple threads caused display issues.
    * Introduced a dedicated `progress_updater` thread that batches updates via a queue and refreshes the progress bar every 1 second.
    * The intermediate deduplication ratio is computed from shared state (`config.fingerprints`, `bytes_total`, etc.) and passed as a postfix dictionary to `tqdm`.
* Implemented `--suppress-result` using a Click flag, suppressing final stdout output when enabled.

## TESTING
* Verified that the `--suppress-result` flag hides the final summary and does not interfere with JSON output generation.
* Confirmed that the progress bar updates once per second and does not flicker or overload the terminal.
* Ensured the intermediate deduplication ratio is visible in the progress bar and updates consistently during scanning.
* Verified final result fields show correct values for:
  * Space Scanned
  * Non-Zero Data Allocated
  * Data Unique
  * Dedup Ratio
* Tested with both file-based and raw disk inputs.
* Ran with and without `--skip-zeroes`.
* Checked compatibility with different thread counts (e.g., 1, 4, 6).
* Ensured the tool still produces valid JSON output.

Fix the race-condition while trying to read config properties moved to Config service. Services `scheduler` and `resource` required some of these properties which are moved to the config service at their startup.

They cannot start unless they get these values, and tomcat cannot continue startup unless these service continue, and these services cannot continue because they need value from config service which cannot respond unless tomcat finish the startup.

This PR reverts the changes from Scheduler service done in #3191
And it removes `DOMAIN` property read in resource service which is not used.

These changes should prevent the startup race condition.

### How to test
1. Check if revert of scheduler service works.
2. Check if tomcat startup does not have any pending boots.

author: yradex
body:
## Summary

### Before this commit

The `lynxViewDidUpdate` callback was consistently not triggered by any data updates.

Previous expectations were that it would be called when data was updated by `updateData()` from client, `resetData()` from client, and JS root component `setData()`. Other data updates, such as those from client `reloadTemplate()` and JS child components `setData()`, also did not trigger the callback.

### With this commit

The `lynxViewDidUpdate` callback will now correctly trigger when data is updated via client `updateData()` and client `resetData()`. Support for JS root component `setData()` (and others) is not yet included in this particular fix.

### Notice

- Even if no data changes are actually processed after calling `updateData()`, the `lynxViewDidUpdate` callback will still be triggered.
- Only one `lynxViewDidUpdate` callback will be triggered per render cycle. Consequently, if multiple `updateData()` calls are made within a single cycle but the data updates are batched, the number of onDataUpdated callbacks triggered may be less than the number of `updateData()` calls.

body:
## Overview
This pull request introduces a comprehensive decentralized merger and acquisition (M&A) due diligence network built on Clarity smart contracts. The system provides end-to-end management of M&A processes from advisor verification to post-merger integration planning.

## New Features

### 1. M&A Advisor Verification System
- **Contract**: `advisor-verification.clar`
- **Features**:
  - Advisor registration and verification workflow
  - Credential and specialization tracking
  - Rating system for advisor performance
  - Deal completion statistics
  - Status management (pending, verified, suspended, revoked)

### 2. Due Diligence Management
- **Contract**: `due-diligence.clar`
- **Features**:
  - Deal creation and lifecycle management
  - Due diligence item tracking and assignment
  - Status updates and completion tracking
  - Multi-party deal coordination (buyer, seller, advisor)
  - Deadline management

### 3. Virtual Data Room Management
- **Contract**: `data-room.clar`
- **Features**:
  - Secure data room creation for each deal
  - Granular access control (none, read, write, admin)
  - Document upload and categorization
  - Access audit trail
  - Hash-based document integrity

### 4. Valuation Coordination
- **Contract**: `valuation-coordination.clar`
- **Features**:
  - Multiple valuation methodology support (DCF, Comparable, Asset-based, Market Multiple)
  - Valuator assignment and management
  - Valuation result submission and approval
  - Confidence level tracking
  - Average valuation calculation

### 5. Integration Planning
- **Contract**: `integration-planning.clar`
- **Features**:
  - Post-merger integration plan creation
  - Milestone tracking with dependencies
  - Team member assignment and role management
  - Priority-based task management
  - Progress tracking and reporting

## Technical Implementation

### Smart Contract Architecture
- **Language**: Clarity
- **Design Pattern**: Modular contract system
- **Data Storage**: Efficient map-based storage for scalability
- **Access Control**: Role-based permissions with multi-level authorization

### Key Data Structures
- Advisor profiles with verification status
- Deal records with multi-party coordination
- Data room access control matrices
- Valuation results with methodology tracking
- Integration milestones with dependency management

### Security Features
- Principal-based authentication
- Role-based access control
- Data integrity through hash verification
- Audit trails for all critical operations
- Multi-signature approval workflows

## Testing Strategy
- Comprehensive unit tests using Vitest
- Contract interaction testing
- Access control validation
- Data integrity verification
- Edge case handling

## Integration Points
- Cross-contract communication for advisor verification
- Data room integration with due diligence processes
- Valuation coordination with deal management
- Integration planning linked to deal completion

## Future Enhancements
- Oracle integration for real-time market data
- Automated compliance checking
- Advanced analytics and reporting
- Mobile application interface
- Integration with traditional M&A platforms

## Breaking Changes
None - This is a new feature implementation.

## Migration Notes
No migration required as this is a new system deployment.

This pull request introduces input validation improvements to both the backend and frontend components of the application. The changes ensure that user inputs are properly validated for correctness and provide helpful feedback when invalid data is entered. Additionally, frontend enhancements improve user experience with better error handling and guidance.

### Backend Validation Enhancements:
* Added a new function `validate_input_row` in `backend/utils/validation.py` to validate individual input rows for `pio2` and `spo2` values. It checks for numeric values and ensures they fall within acceptable ranges.
* Updated the `predict` function in `backend/app.py` to validate each input row using explicit checks for format, numeric values, and value ranges. Errors are returned with descriptive messages for invalid inputs.
* Imported the `validate_input_row` function in `backend/app.py` for use in validation logic.

### Frontend Validation Enhancements:
* Added utility functions `spo2OutOfRange` and `pio2OutOfRange` in `frontend/src/utils/validation.js` to check if `spo2` and `pio2` values are out of range or invalid.
* Integrated validation logic into `PredictForm.js` to display error messages and helper text for invalid `spo2` and `pio2` inputs directly in the form fields. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-af5f36ff63d7d52047ee9c44435c05625406a5c9807bd9c2250892ef39e94403R104-R128) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-af5f36ff63d7d52047ee9c44435c05625406a5c9807bd9c2250892ef39e94403R137-R161)
* Disabled the "Submit" button in `PredictForm.js` when any input field contains invalid data, ensuring users cannot proceed with erroneous entries. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-af5f36ff63d7d52047ee9c44435c05625406a5c9807bd9c2250892ef39e94403R27-R35) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-af5f36ff63d7d52047ee9c44435c05625406a5c9807bd9c2250892ef39e94403L116-R185)

### User Experience Improvements:
* Added a note in `PredictForm.js` to guide users on optimal input ranges for better model performance.
* Adjusted the prediction output in `PredictForm.js` to display uncertainty values rounded to two decimal places for improved readability.

body:
## Summary

This PR implements TypeScript Project References to solve persistent type checking issues in the monorepo, particularly with `@claude-nexus/shared` imports.

## Problem

The monorepo was experiencing "Cannot find module '@claude-nexus/shared' or its corresponding type declarations" errors during type checking, even though the code compiled and ran correctly with Bun. This was due to circular dependencies where the shared package needed to be built before services could type check.

## Solution

Implemented TypeScript Project References as recommended by a consensus workflow with multiple AI models. This provides:

- Automatic dependency resolution and build ordering
- Incremental builds for better performance
- Proper monorepo support with cross-package imports
- Better IDE support with improved IntelliSense

## Changes

### Configuration Updates
- ✅ Updated all `tsconfig.json` files to use composite projects
- ✅ Enabled declaration generation for cross-package imports
- ✅ Created root `tsconfig.json` with references to all packages

### Script Updates
- ✅ Replaced `bun x tsc --noEmit` with `tsc --build` in all typecheck scripts
- ✅ Updated package.json scripts to use TypeScript's build mode

### Bug Fixes
- ✅ Added missing `body` field to `ApiRequest` interface in storage reader
- ✅ Exported `DomainTokenStats` interface for proper type inference

### Documentation
- ✅ Created ADR-013 documenting this architectural decision
- ✅ Updated CLAUDE.md with new typecheck approach and reference to ADR

## Testing

- Ran `bun run typecheck` - all checks pass ✅
- Ran `bun run format` - all files formatted ✅
- Built shared package to generate declaration files

## Impact

This change maintains full compatibility with Bun's runtime while leveraging TypeScript's built-in features for better monorepo support. No changes to runtime behavior or build outputs.

body:
This PR implements comprehensive support for Kubefleet's ClusterResourcePlacement manifests in Draft, enabling users to generate both PickAll and PickFixed placement type manifests as requested in the issue.

## New Features

### Kubefleet ClusterResourcePlacement Template
Added `kubefleet-clusterresourceplacement` addon template that supports:
- `metadata.name` configuration via `CRP_NAME` variable
- `spec.resourceSelectors.name` configuration via `RESOURCE_SELECTOR_NAME` variable  
- `policy.placementType` configuration via `PLACEMENT_TYPE` variable (PickAll/PickFixed)
- `policy.clusterNames` configuration via `CLUSTER_NAME_1` and `CLUSTER_NAME_2` variables for PickFixed type
- Standard Draft labels and metadata patterns

### Usage Examples

**PickAll placement type:**
```bash
draft update --addon kubefleet-clusterresourceplacement \
  --variable CRP_NAME=demo-crp \
  --variable RESOURCE_SELECTOR_NAME=fmad-demo \
  --variable PLACEMENT_TYPE=PickAll \
  --variable PARTOF=my-project
```

Generates the exact YAML from the first sample in the issue:
```yaml
apiVersion: placement.kubernetes-fleet.io/v1
kind: ClusterResourcePlacement
metadata:
  name: demo-crp
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: demo-crp
    app.kubernetes.io/part-of: my-project
    kubernetes.azure.com/generator: draft
spec:
  resourceSelectors:
    - group: ""
      kind: Namespace
      name: fmad-demo
      version: v1
  policy:
    placementType: PickAll
```

**PickFixed placement type:**
```bash
draft update --addon kubefleet-clusterresourceplacement \
  --variable CRP_NAME=fmad-demo-crp \
  --variable RESOURCE_SELECTOR_NAME=fmad-demo \
  --variable PLACEMENT_TYPE=PickFixed \
  --variable CLUSTER_NAME_1=cluster-name-01 \
  --variable CLUSTER_NAME_2=cluster-name-02 \
  --variable PARTOF=my-project
```

Generates the exact YAML from the second sample in the issue with cluster names array.

## Bug Fixes

### Fixed `draft update --addon` Parameter
- The `--addon` parameter was previously ignored, always defaulting to `app-routing-ingress`
- Now properly uses the specified addon template while maintaining backward compatibility
- When no `--addon` is specified, still defaults to `app-routing-ingress` for existing workflows

### Fixed ActiveWhen Constraint Handling
- Fixed prompts system to check `activeWhen` constraints before checking for disabled prompts
- Resolves issue where conditional variables (like cluster names for PickFixed) were incorrectly required in non-interactive mode
- Variables that are inactive due to `activeWhen` constraints are now properly skipped

## Testing

- Comprehensive test suite with fixtures for both PickAll and PickFixed scenarios
- Template validation passes all existing checks
- Backward compatibility verified for existing `app-routing-ingress` addon
- All existing tests continue to pass

## Documentation

Added comprehensive documentation at `docs/kubefleet-clusterresourceplacement.md` with:
- Usage examples for both placement types
- Variable reference table
- Interactive and non-interactive mode instructions

body:
## Summary

Implements Phase 1 of the async jobs framework to standardize long-running operations in MCP tools.

• AsyncJob abstract base class with cancellation support
• JobManager with concurrency control and background execution  
• JobResult and JobProgress data structures
• InMemoryJobStore implementation with automatic cleanup
• Comprehensive error handling and logging

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for all core components (models, job base class, store, manager)
- [x] Integration tests with real-world scenarios
- [x] Test coverage for error conditions and edge cases
- [x] Type safety validation with mypy-compatible type hints

## Key Features

**Token-based Job Tracking**: Each job gets a unique token for status monitoring and result retrieval

**Graceful Cancellation**: Jobs can be cancelled mid-execution with proper resource cleanup

**Progress Tracking**: Built-in progress reporting for long-running operations

**Concurrency Control**: Configurable limits on concurrent job execution with semaphore-based throttling

**Automatic Cleanup**: TTL-based result storage with background cleanup tasks

**Type Safety**: Full type hints throughout for better development experience

## Framework Benefits

- Eliminates code duplication across MCP tools with async operations
- Provides consistent interfaces for clients using long-running commands  
- Standardizes error handling and progress reporting patterns
- Enables better resource management and monitoring

## Implementation Location

All code is located under `/utils/async_jobs/` with complete documentation in `/mcp_tools/docs/async_job_framework.md`

author: teogeb
body:
## Summary

Entries in the undelegation queue now affect the Autostaker calculations. 

## Background
 
When a delegator undelegates some amount from an operator, the tokens aren't immediately transferred back to the delegator. Instead the amount is added to the undelegation queue. The transfer happens as soon as there are enough unstaked tokens in the operator contract.

## Changes

Modified the target stake calculation `payoutProportionalStrategy`. The rounding logic and skipping of small transactions are also affected slightly. The autostaker plugin reads the sum of undelegation queue entries from The Graph and passes the amount to the strategy function.

Also added more assertions to the `autostaker.test.ts` smoke tests.

## Other changes

- The `myStakedAmount` in calculated from the stakes instead of querying it from the contract
- Simplified logging in the plugin

## Chores

- Removed `sum.ts` from the `@streamr/utils` package
  - it was not exported
  - the file was added during the development of https://github.com/streamr-dev/network/pull/3086 (we should have removed the file in that PR)
- Fixed field type in `StakeQueryResultItem`

body:
This PR implements the requested `publish` Git alias that allows users to push their current branch to origin with upstream tracking set up in a single command.

## Changes Made

### Core Implementation
- Added `alias.publish` to the git-config.ps1 settings array with the value:
  ```
  !git push --set-upstream origin $(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
  ```

### Documentation Updates
- Updated the `setup-git` function documentation to include the new `publish` alias
- Added the alias to the git-config/README.md features list and settings table
- Documented the alias functionality: "Pushes current branch with upstream setup"

## Usage

After running `setup-git`, users can now use:
```bash
git publish
```

This command will:
1. Get the current branch name using `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`
2. Push the branch to origin with `--set-upstream` flag
3. Set up tracking so future `git push` and `git pull` commands work seamlessly

## Testing

- Verified the alias is correctly set in Git global configuration
- Tested that the setup-git function runs without errors
- Confirmed the alias command resolves to the expected Git command
- Validated that existing aliases continue to work properly

This enhancement improves the developer workflow by eliminating the need to manually specify upstream tracking when pushing new branches.

author: copilot
body:
Fixed the issue where X and O game pieces appeared white on white background, making them invisible to players.

## Problem
From the meeting notes: "We need to make the crosses black because we can't see them because they're white on white."

The game cells had a white background (`background: #fff`) but no explicit text color was set for the X and O pieces, causing visibility issues.

## Solution
Added explicit black color (`color: #000`) to the `.cell` CSS rule to ensure both X and O are clearly visible against the white cell backgrounds.

**Change Made:**
```css
/* Before */
.cell { width: 80px; height: 80px; background: #fff; border: 2px solid #333; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 2.5rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s; }

/* After */
.cell { width: 80px; height: 80px; background: #fff; border: 2px solid #333; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 2.5rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s; color: #000; }
```

This minimal change ensures optimal contrast and visibility for all game pieces without affecting any other functionality.

Fixes #17.

author: copilot
body:
Implements support for parsing XSD reference types as requested in issue #170, replacing the previous `anydata` placeholder approach with proper type references.

## Problem
Previously, XSD elements with `ref` attributes or custom type references were not properly parsed, leading to the use of `anydata` as a placeholder. This prevented proper type tracking and code generation with specific type aliases.

## Solution
Following approach 1 from the issue (preferred), this PR adds `ReferenceType` as a new `XSDType` implementation that can be converted to type aliases during code generation.

### Key Changes

1. **Added `ReferenceType` record**
   - New sealed interface implementation of `XSDType`
   - Stores reference name and integrates with existing type tracking

2. **Enhanced XSD element parsing**
   - Modified `parseXSDXElement` to handle `ref` attribute
   - Falls back to `ReferenceType` for unknown custom types
   - Preserves existing basic type and complex type parsing

3. **Updated type conversion**
   - Added support in `ConversionUtils.toTypeDesc()` for `ReferenceType`
   - Converts to `BallerinaModel.TypeDesc.TypeReference` with namespace stripping
   - Enables proper type alias generation

4. **Comprehensive testing**
   - Tests for ref attribute parsing: `<element ref="tns:CommonType"/>`
   - Tests for custom type handling: `<element type="tns:CustomType"/>`
   - Integration tests for conversion to TypeReference

### Example Usage
```xml
<!-- Now properly parsed as ReferenceType -->
<element ref="tns:CommonType" minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="1"/>
<element name="CustomElement" type="tns:CustomType"/>
```

The implementation integrates seamlessly with the existing `ProjectAnalysisContext` type tracking and resolution mechanisms, requiring no changes to the analysis infrastructure.

Fixes #170.

author: ajanzhong
body:
pkg/boot/universalpayload: Update PCI Root Bridge fetch logic
Previous, PCI Root Bridge info is constructed from all resource files
in /sys/bus/pci/devices folder, it applies to single segment platform.

In order to support multiple segments platform, we need to get PCI
hierarchy from /sys/devices/pci* device nodes. Since PCI device nodes
under this format of path are align with actual PCI hierarchy.

For instance, following is hierarchy snippet from command "lspci -t":
 \-[0000:00]-+-00.0
      +-1c.0-[01]--+-00.0
                   \-00.1
      +-1c.5-[03-04]----00.0-[04]----00.0

Corresponding device nodes layout in /sys/devices/pci* are as follows:
  /sys/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:1c.0/0000:01:00.0
  /sys/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:1c.5/0000:03:00.0/0000:04:00.0

body:
## Why I'm doing:

```sql
CREATE
MATERIALIZED VIEW mv_test99
REFRESH ASYNC EVERY(INTERVAL 60 MINUTE)
PARTITION BY p_time
PROPERTIES (
"partition_refresh_number" = "1"
)
AS
select date_trunc("day", a.datekey) as p_time, sum(a.v1) as value
from par_tbl1 a
group by p_time, a.item_id
union all
select date_trunc('day', date_add(b.datekey, INTERVAL 1 DAY)) AS p_time, sum(b.v1) as value
from par_tbl1 b
group by p_time, item_id
;
```

The query result of this view is wrong because one partition is refreshed less.


## What I'm doing:

Fixes #59203


1. Save the remaining expressions of the `union` MV.
2. When refreshing the MV, calculate how many virtual partitions we need to add to the MV.
3. Save the newly added virtual partition to the MV separately.
4. After the calculation incremental partition is completed, add the virtual partition to the partition that needs to be refreshed.

- AI paddle follows ball with controlled delay for fair gameplay

## 📱 Responsive Design

The game automatically adapts to different screen sizes:
- **Desktop**: Full-featured layout with optimal canvas size
- **Tablet**: Adjusted proportions while maintaining playability  
- **Mobile**: Compact layout with touch-friendly interface

### Ball Physics
```javascript
// Angle variation based on paddle hit position
const hitPos = (ball.y - (paddle.y + paddle.height / 2)) / (paddle.height / 2);
ball.speedY = hitPos * 8; // Creates realistic bounce angles

```javascript
// AI follows ball with realistic reaction time
if (paddleCenter < ballY - 35) {

}
```

2. Press **Space** to start the game

author: msxuc
body:
Main changes:
- Refactored tensor_group_partition pass, adjusted how we distribute the adjmat for distpart/METIS.
  - Previously we simply-and-conceptually concat all TensorGroups and then evenly distribute the adjmat, the main issue is that the calculation for this is complex, also, this leads to unbalanced distribution of nonzero entities in the adjmat.
  - Now we evenly distribute each TensorGroup and each worker has one piece of each TensorGroup.
- Introduce a general mechanism `dist_env.unbalanced_compute_heartbeat` to avoid collective call timeout due to unbalanced workload.
  - The timeout happens when some workers have lighter workload and enter the collective call earlier. If other workers take a long time to finish calculate, the workers who entered earlier would timeout. Instead of manually and ad hoc configuring the timeout threshold, we'll stably keep communication environment healthy.
  - All heavy, possible unbalanced workloads are now guarded by `unbalanced_compute_heartbeat`.

body:
This PR implements comprehensive documentation and UI support for remote hubs (cross-tenant) functionality in FinOps hubs.

## Problem
Remote hubs support was added to the backend infrastructure but was never fully documented or accessible through the UI deployment form. Users had no guidance on how to configure cross-tenant scenarios where satellite hubs send data to a central primary hub.

## Solution

### 1. UI Form Enhancement
- Added **Remote hub configuration** section to the Advanced step in `createUiDefinition.json`
- Added `remoteHubStorageUri` field with Data Lake storage URI validation
- Added `remoteHubStorageKey` field as secure password input with storage key validation
- Properly configured outputs to pass parameters to the deployment template

### 2. Comprehensive Documentation
- Added new section **"Optional: Configure remote hubs"** to the main deployment guide
- Documented when to use remote hubs (multi-tenant scenarios)
- Explained architecture with primary and satellite hub concepts
- Provided step-by-step configuration for both Azure portal and PowerShell
- Included security considerations and best practices

### 3. PowerShell Documentation Updates
- Updated `Deploy-FinOpsHub` command syntax to include remote hub parameters
- Enhanced parameters table with detailed descriptions and examples
- Added complete deployment example for remote hub scenarios

### 4. Enhanced Template Documentation
- Improved parameter descriptions for `remoteHubStorageUri` and `remoteHubStorageKey`
- Added clear instructions for obtaining values from the primary hub
- Documented version requirements (0.4+) and security implications

## Key Features
- **Cross-tenant support**: Enable cost data aggregation across multiple Azure tenants
- **Secure configuration**: Proper handling of storage keys as secure parameters
- **Complete guidance**: End-to-end instructions for both portal and PowerShell deployment
- **Architecture clarity**: Clear explanation of primary vs satellite hub roles

## Configuration Parameters
- `remoteHubStorageUri`: Data Lake storage endpoint from primary hub (e.g., `https://primaryhub.dfs.core.windows.net/`)
- `remoteHubStorageKey`: Storage account access key from primary hub

## Usage Example
```powershell
Deploy-FinOpsHub `
    -Name MyRemoteHub `
    -ResourceGroup MyRemoteHubResourceGroup `
    -Location westus `
    -RemoteHubStorageUri "https://centralhub.dfs.core.windows.net/" `
    -RemoteHubStorageKey "storage-key-here"
```

The backend implementation already existed - this PR completes the user-facing documentation and UI integration to make remote hubs fully accessible and properly documented.

Fixes #1093.

The changes focus on creating reusable composite actions for building, pushing, and scanning Docker images, enhancing security permissions, and simplifying Dockerfile configurations. Below is a summary of the key changes grouped by theme:

### New Composite Actions for Docker Operations:
* Added `.github/actions/docker-build-and-push/action.yaml` to create a reusable action for building and pushing Docker images to `ghcr.io`. This action supports configurable inputs like `dockerfile`, `image-name`, `image-tag`, and `build-args` and provides the image digest as an output.
* Added `.github/actions/docker-scan/action.yaml` to create a reusable action for scanning Docker images with vulnerability reports and SBOM generation. This action integrates tools like `syft`, `cosign`, and `Grype` and allows uploading SARIF results to GitHub.

### Workflow Enhancements:
* Updated multiple workflows (e.g., `build-admin-portal.yaml`, `build-authorization.yaml`, `build-certificates.yaml`) to include enhanced permissions for actions, attestations, contents, and security events. This ensures proper access control for workflows. body:
## Overview
This PR introduces a comprehensive blockchain-based corporate governance system consisting of five independent smart contracts designed to manage various aspects of corporate board operations.

## Contracts Implemented

### 1. Board Secretary Verification Contract
- **File**: `contracts/board-secretary-verification.clar`
- **Purpose**: Validates and manages corporate board secretaries
- **Key Features**:
  - Secretary registration and verification
  - Authority validation
  - Secretary status management

### 2. Meeting Coordination Contract
- **File**: `contracts/meeting-coordination.clar`
- **Purpose**: Coordinates and manages board meetings
- **Key Features**:
  - Meeting scheduling
  - Attendance tracking
  - Meeting status management

### 3. Decision Tracking Contract
- **File**: `contracts/decision-tracking.clar`
- **Purpose**: Records and tracks board decisions
- **Key Features**:
  - Decision proposal creation
  - Voting mechanism
  - Decision history tracking

### 4. Compliance Monitoring Contract
- **File**: `contracts/compliance-monitoring.clar`
- **Purpose**: Monitors governance compliance requirements
- **Key Features**:
  - Compliance rule definition
  - Violation tracking
  - Compliance status reporting

### 5. Shareholder Communication Contract
- **File**: `contracts/shareholder-communication.clar`
- **Purpose**: Manages communications with shareholders
- **Key Features**:
  - Message broadcasting
  - Shareholder registration
  - Communication history

## Technical Implementation
- **Language**: Clarity smart contracts
- **Architecture**: Independent contracts with no cross-references
- **Testing**: Comprehensive test suite using Vitest
- **Security**: Input validation and access control mechanisms

## Testing Strategy
Each contract includes comprehensive unit tests covering:
- Core functionality
- Edge cases
- Error handling
- Access control

## Deployment Considerations
- Each contract can be deployed independently
- No dependencies between contracts
- Suitable for modular deployment strategies

author: erisu
body:
<!--
Please make sure the checklist boxes are all checked before submitting the PR. The checklist is intended as a quick reference, for complete details please see our Contributor Guidelines:

http://cordova.apache.org/contribute/contribute_guidelines.html

Thanks!
-->

### Motivation and Context
<!-- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
<!-- If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here. -->

- Add partial support for Night & Day Theming.
- Prefix Cordova core resource values with `cdv_*` to avoid issues caused by plugins that either create or modify the same files.

This should also:

Resolves #1485

Cover SplashScreen & Background Color. (SystemBars, such as Status Bar & Gesture/Navigation Bar, will be handled in a separate PR)

### Description
<!-- Describe your changes in detail -->

- `res/values/cdv_colors.xml`
  - A rename from `colors.xml`.
  - `cdv_background_color` set to `#FAF8FF`. Same values as SDK 34+.
  - `cdv_splashscreen_background` set to `@color/cdv_background_color` to match background color.
- `res/values-v34/cdv_colors.xml`
  - New file
  - `cdv_background_color` set to `@android:color/system_background_light`.
  - `cdv_splashscreen_background` set to `@color/cdv_background_color` to match background color.
- `res/values-night/cdv_colors.xml`
  - New file
  - `cdv_background_color` set to `#121318`. Same values as SDK 34+.
  - `cdv_splashscreen_background` set to `@color/cdv_background_color` to match background color.
- `res/values-night-v34/cdv_colors.xml`
  - New file
  - `cdv_background_color` set to `@android:color/system_background_dark`.
  - `cdv_splashscreen_background` set to `@color/cdv_background_color` to match background color.
- `res/values/cdv_themes.xml`
  - A rename from `themes.xml`.
  - New `postSplashScreenTheme` default value `@style/Theme.Cordova.App.DayNight`.
  - `Theme.Cordova.App.DayNight` new theme with `android:colorBackground` set to `@color/cdv_background_color`
- `res/values/cdv_strings.xml`
  - A rename from `cdv_strings.xml`.

SplashScreen background color can be set by the following preferences, in the order of priority:

 - `AndroidWindowSplashScreenBackground`
 - `SplashScreenBackgroundColor`
 - `BackgroundColor`

Previously when the preferences was set and `cordova prepare` was executed, `colors.xml` would have been updated.
Now, `cdv_themes.xml` would be updated instead with the `#RRGGBB` or `#AARRGGBB` value inserted into the SplashScreens `windowSplashScreenBackground`. Since Cordova only accepted one color value for the SplashScreen background, it was easier to change the theme instead of the four colors resource files.

### Testing
<!-- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes. -->

- `npm t`
- Build App
- Tried setting preferences to another color.

author: lnkuiper
body:
Similar to the `cast_to_type` utility function, this PR implements the `replace_type` function, which can replace types _within_ nested types. For example:
```sql
SELECT replace_type({
    duck: 3.141592653589793::DOUBLE,
    goose: 2.718281828459045::DOUBLE
}, NULL::DOUBLE, NULL::DECIMAL(15,2)) AS r;
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        r                        │
│ struct(duck decimal(15,2), goose decimal(15,2)) │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ {'duck': 3.14, 'goose': 2.72}                   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
It conditionally casts a column of a specified type to a column of another specified type, in this case, it casts from `DOUBLE` to `DECIMAL(15,2)`. It also works on non-nested types, in which case it pretty much does this:
```sql
SELECT CASE WHEN (c) == '<TYPE1>' THEN C::<TYPE2> ELSE C END;
```

body: Fixes https://github.com/elastic/sdh-kibana/issues/5541 ## Summary When the user had `xpack.ml.enabled` set to false, the ES deprecation list was throwing the error `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')`. This was caused because UA was expecting to always receive an ML array in the migration deprecation response. ![Screenshot 2025-06-27 at 13 43 38](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d8a05d07-bd1c-4627-b7ca-9e6b6ccc90ca) This PR makes the ES list not to fail when the user has this disabled. However, I wasn't able to test what would happen if the cluster contains ML deprecations but the setting is set to false and the user upgrades it and then enables it again. For that reason, at least for the moment, this PR also introduces a callout informing of this feature to be disabled: Also, this way, if some migration for ML fails, the user is informed of the root cause. For instance, for System indices: ### How to test * Follow the instructions in https://github.com/elastic/kibana-team/issues/1521. Use the data folder named `data_qaf_7.17.zip`. This contains ML deprecations. * Run ES and Kibana as usual for Upgrade Assistant. Verify that the callout is not present. * Run ES for UA but adding the flag `-E xpack.ml.enabled=false` and Kibana as usual. * Verify the plugin loads. * Verify the Es deprecation list does not contain ML deprecations. * Verify that the callout is present.

author: avirtopeanu-ionos
body:
Overhauls the config subsystem to support our new SDK YAML format, deprecating the old JSON config.

To avoid breaking changes, the credentials found in old config file will now be copied over to the new `yaml` format, but only if no new config file is found. This doesn't delete the old config file however, and also prints a deprecation notice. 

Adds support for overriding location-specific endpoints per product based on config file settings

The `login` command now generates a YAML config file based on the IONOS API index

Adds `login --example` to generate a new sample YAML config file to stdout 

Adds 'filtering' functionality to `login` command: version, visibility, gate, whitelist/blacklist, custom naming

`whoami` related authentication priorities have been re-done to reflect the new config file, and remove mentions of old --token which only had relevance in the `login` command anyway
```
Authentication layers, in order of priority:
  [1] environment variable: IONOS_TOKEN
  [2] environment variables: IONOS_USERNAME, IONOS_PASSWORD
  [3] credentials from config file: token
  [4] credentials from config file: username, password
```

`logout` has been improved to prompt for deletion of legacy .json if located in the same directory as the new .yaml config file and has expected content 

Updated 'location' command as well as client location priorities, as such:   '--config' value > 'IONOS_CONFIG_FILE' > SDK config file ('~/.ionos/config'). To not induce breaking changes, if no config file is found, we still print the value of '--config' flag (or the default if not set)

Updated client package to re-generate parts of the client if we detect a new desired URL , This is not the most efficient solution in the world, and might be re-visited in the future

Added `WithRegionalConfigOverride` and `WithConfigOverride` which propagate the config file settings based on the desired product from the config file. These also automatically set certain help text values, for example:
```
% ionosctl dns
...(help-text)...
FLAGS:
  -u, --api-url string    Override default host URL. If contains placeholder, location will be embedded. Preferred over the config file override 'dns' and env var 'IONOS_API_URL' (default "https://dns.%s.ionos.com")
  -l, --location string   Location of the resource to operate on. Can be one of: de/fra (default "de/fra")
...(help-text)...
```

which also informs the user which config file entry he needs to modify for that command

Adds a full coverage of these cases to user.bats tests

body:
## 概要
v0.1.9でアプリが起動時に以下のエラーで失敗する問題を修正します：
```
Fatal error: could not load resource bundle: from /ClaudeCodeMonitor.app/ClaudeCodeMonitor_ClaudeCodeMonitor.bundle
```

## 問題の原因
SwiftPMが生成する`resource_bundle_accessor.swift`は、実行ファイルと同じディレクトリにリソースバンドルがあることを期待していますが、macOSアプリでは`Contents/Resources`に配置する必要があります。

この問題は、[v20250625-120023からv0.1.9への変更](https://github.com/K9i-0/ClaudeCodeMonitor/compare/v20250625-120023...v0.1.9)で導入されたバグです。タグベースのバージョン管理システムへの移行時に、リソースバンドルのパス解決が正しく動作しなくなりました。

## 解決策
1. **ResourceBundleヘルパーの実装**
   - `Localization.swift`に複数のパスを試すヘルパーを追加
   - macOSアプリ構造（Contents/Resources）を優先的に確認
   - フォールバックとして既存のBundle.moduleも使用

2. **ビルドプロセスの改善**
   - アプリバンドル作成処理を`scripts/create-app-bundle.sh`に分離
   - GitHub Actionsワークフローを簡素化
   - メンテナンス性の向上

- [x] リソース（ローカライゼーション）が正しく読み込まれることを確認

author: twilightzebby
body:
While the actual Role Menus, when posted in Channels for Server Members to use, have already been updated to use Components v2 - the preview of Role Menus *(shown during creation/configuration)* haven't.

This PR updates that preview to use Components v2. Thus, being a more accurate preview to what actually gets posted upon saving the Role Menu.

This PR also aims to make this module fully stateless, since I can*not* for the *life* of me get CloudFlare Workers to extend the lifetime of a Worker.[^1]

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This PR will be be https://github.com/TwilightZebby/TwiLite/labels/blocked from merging until *both* String Selects *and* Role Selects/Inputs have been added to App Modals by Discord's Apps & API Team.[^2]

[^1]: From experience, CloudFlare Workers only live for about 3-5 seconds maximum per received request. Which means, my "local cache" for the Role Menu system gets deleted after 3-5 seconds, which is the reason why TwiLite throws errors when someone takes longer than that *per action* during Role Menu creation/configuration. Also, that `ctx.waitUntil()` method doesn't seem to do SHIT when I try to use it to extend the Worker's lifetime!

[^2]: Currently, TwiLite uses a local cache to temp-store Role Menu data, including the data of the first Interaction Response, in order to get/edit said Interaction Response with the updated previews. In order to do this fully stateless, without the need of local caches or databases, I would need to be able to fetch/edit the first Interaction Response using only data that Discord's API returns. Which is not possible right now. However, Discord's Apps & API Team are currently updating App Modals to add more component support for Modals, so this PR will not be mergeable until Discord supports what I need in Modals!

This pull request introduces significant updates to the frontend codebase, focusing on feature enhancements, code cleanup, and bug fixes. Key changes include improvements to the `ToastNotification` component, updates to the `AdminView` layout, and the addition of new DAO methods for handling activities, clubs, and finances.

* **`frontend/src/components/ui/ToastNotification.vue`**: Added support for a new notification type (`warning`) and implemented entry/exit animations for better user experience.

### Layout Enhancements:
* **`frontend/src/layouts/AdminView.vue`**: Refactored to include proper imports for `useClubStore`, removed unused imports, and updated the sidebar and header to dynamically display club details.
* **`frontend/src/layouts/LoginView.vue`**: Corrected the view to focus solely on login functionality, removing content mistakenly added from `HomeView`.

### DAO Additions:
* **`frontend/src/services/dao/ActivityDao.ts`**: Expanded the DAO with methods for fetching activities by group, creating/updating activities, and deleting activities.
* **`frontend/src/services/dao/ClubDao.ts`**: Added a method to fetch club details and updated the method for modifying club settings.
* **`frontend/src/services/dao/FinanceDao.ts`**: Introduced a new DAO for managing club finances, including methods for fetching summaries, listing transactions, and adding new transactions.

body:
This PR will prefer the connection info credentials instead of the password file.

In old nexus versions that file was only created if the admin didn't had a (custom) password set. In recent versions that file get's always created but login is not possible if the password was changed.

In result this module had problems creating resources as the api calls failed because of 401.

We now default to provided credentials and only fall back to the password file if login didn't work. This is only used for the very first run of puppet usually.

Fixes #71

author: oleg-ssvlabs
body:
During the SSV node test with the increased number of validators (**3k**), a few bottlenecks were identified. These bottlenecks increase the time required for consensus and duty execution overall. The main issues were observed in the **Process Consensus** and **Process Post Consensus** phases.

This PR attempts to optimize the **Process Consensus** phase by parallelizing execution using goroutines.

Improvement(**2846** validator cluster):
Duty duration (`ssv.validator.execute_committee_duty` trace):
previously - median `499.5 ms`

with unlimited concurrency - median `421ms`
with 30 concurrent workers - median `440ms`

### What change is being made?

Refactor metabox and shortcode initialization by removing `add_action` hooks and executing them directly in `loader.php` for both the Quiz and Summary modules.

author: quangvdao
body:
1. Re-arrange the ordering of type / variable declaration, so that it goes `oSpec` => `StmtIn` => `OStmtIn` => `WitIn` => `StmtOut` => `OStmtOut` => `WitOut` => `pSpec`. Note that protocol specification now goes at the end.

The underlying logic is that we want to order things in terms of potential dependencies on each other (future refactors may need to do this). So the underlying monad / oracle computation should always stay the same, then takes in the input / output interface (with input statement first), and then finally specify the protocol structure.

2. Refactor lenses both in terms of names but also in terms of defining them directly as `PFunctor.Lens`

3. Refactor sequential composition to start from the empty protocol, allowing indexing to go for `(n : Fin m → ℕ)` instead of `(n : Fin (m + 1) → ℕ)`.

4. Refactor security notions into multiple files, with round-by-round and state-restoration into separate files

5. Other minor refactors (name changes, moving things around)

6. Fix existing (oracle) reductions to account for the above refactors

author: khanaffan
body:
imodel-native: https://github.com/iTwin/imodel-native/pull/1162

### **Issue Summary**

1. **Initial Changeset Push**:  
   OpenSite+ modified the GCS and pushed a changeset.

2. **Schema Import by Civil Connector**:  
   Civil Connector imported a schema and made additional GCS changes.

3. **PullMerge Failure in OpenSite+**:  
   OpenSite+ (with no local changes) attempted a `PullMerge()`, which failed due to the following sequence:
   - A schema changeset was applied.
   - `TxnManager` disables tracking during `applyChangeset()`, but afterward, it recomputes `ec_cache_*` tables, which **are** tracked.
   - `pullMergeEnd()` calls `saveChanges()`, creating a transaction.
   - A subsequent changeset apply detects a rebase is needed.
     - During rebase, it tries to undo the transaction containing `ec_cache_*` changes.
     - This fails with a **FOREIGN_KEY_CONSTRAINT** error.
     - The failure occurs because `ec_cache_*` tables reference `ec_class` via foreign keys. Reverting the cache tables leads to missing parent `ec_class` entries.

---

### **Solution**

1. **Exclude `ec_cache_*` from Tracking**:  
   These tables are derived and can be safely recomputed, so they should not be tracked.

2. **Disable `NOFKCONSTRAINT` Flag for Schema Changesets**:  
   Since `ec_cache_*` tables have FK relationships to `ec_class` and `ec_table`, cascading deletes must be allowed. This ensures that when primary tables are modified, related cache entries are also cleaned up properly.

---

### **Additional Safeguard**

- A warning has been added to flag any local changes detected during `PullMergeEnd()`, as ideally, there should be none.

body:
This convenience method makes it easier to use the YaraScanner with a Python defined YARA rule. This makes one off, single file plugins easier to make because one can include the YARA rule directly in Python instead of having to include the rule in a separate YARA file. I.e.:

```python

RULE = """rule ExampleRule
{
    strings:
        $line = { 00 01 02 03 }

    condition:
        all of them
}
"""

class Plugin:
    [setup]
    
    def _generator(self, layer):
        rule = yarascan.YaraScanner.from_text(RULE)
        scanner = yarascan.YaraScanner(rules=rule)
        [...]
""""

author: achirkin
body:
When CAGRA graph is not host accessible, HNSW::from_cagra routine copies the data from it to the base layer of HNSW in two stages: first to a host matrix, then to the HNSW index object. As a result, the graph, which can be huge, is allocated in the host memory twice.
For big enough graphs this manifests itself in the program being killed by the linux kernel at the end of the index building process due to not enough system memory.

This PR avoids the staging graph buffer by using cudaMemcpy2DAsync to copy the data in an appropriate format in one go.

author: mike-turintech
body:
This commit introduces several key improvements to the `Single` class methods to enhance performance, robustness, and clarity.

- **`sumRange(int n)`:** Replaced array-based calculation with a direct mathematical formula (`n * (n - 1) / 2`), significantly improving performance by avoiding unnecessary allocations and loops.
- **`maxArray(int[] arr)`:** Added defensive checks for `null` or empty arrays and corrected initialization of `max` to `arr[0]` to handle negative numbers correctly. The loop now starts from the second element.
- **`sumModulus(int n, int m)`:** Replaced the legacy `java.util.Vector` and stream API with a simple iterative loop for summing, improving performance and memory efficiency while removing unused imports.

These changes collectively make the code more efficient, reliable, and maintainable.



<details>
<summary>Detailed Score Information</summary>

### Score Details

This section contains detailed information about the performance scores for top 5 scored suggestions.

## Top Performing Changes

### 1. app/src/main/java/control/Single.java:1-57 - Mean Improvement: 0.80, Mean Original Score: 2.72

- 🔴 **Compatibility** (Change: -0.60): The changes slightly affect backward compatibility for the method maxArray, as it now throws an IllegalArgumentException for null or empty arrays, whereas the original would return 0. The other methods (sumRange and sumModulus) are compatible and improve implementation without affecting signatures or expected input-output for valid inputs.

- 🔴 **Equivalence** (Change: -0.25): sumRange and sumModulus remain functionally equivalent but with more efficient implementations. maxArray now throws an exception for empty or null input, which is a behavioral change for those specific cases, but for all valid inputs the function is otherwise equivalent. Thus, the general logic and expected outputs for normal use are preserved.

- 🟢 **Performance** (Change: +1.90): The changes provide significant performance improvements across all methods. First, sumRange() now uses the mathematical formula n*(n-1)/2 instead of creating and populating an array, eliminating O(n) space complexity and reducing time complexity. The sumModulus() method now directly accumulates the sum instead of creating a Vector collection and using stream operations, which avoids unnecessary object creation and processing overhead. This approach is much more efficient for large values of n. The maxArray() method now avoids unnecessary array element access by starting at index 1 and comparing directly in the array.

- 🟢 **Quality** (Score: 4.75; Change: +1.75): The code is significantly improved for quality. Comments are enhanced to explain optimizations, unnecessary imports and data structures are removed, error checking for null or empty arrays is added, and methods are simplified for both readability and maintainability. The logic is easier to follow and less error-prone. The maxArray function now properly handles all int arrays. The intent of each calculation is clear and idiomatic.

- 🟢 **Value** (Change: +2.00): The changes significantly improve the code in multiple ways. First, the sumRange method is replaced with a mathematical formula (n*(n-1)/2) which is far more efficient than allocating and populating an array. The maxArray method now handles edge cases by checking for null/empty arrays and initializes max with the first element (fixing a bug with negative numbers). The sumModulus method replaces the inefficient Vector collection and stream with a simple accumulator, improving performance and reducing memory overhead. All changes make the code more robust, efficient, and maintainable without changing functionality.


</details>

body:
Refactor the `SupplyProcessor` and `GridProcessor` to make results processing easier to navigate. After refactoring I will fix existing issues in the results and results display. Will close #86.

I did some restructuring to define the output KPIs inside a `csv` file instead of the code, so `python manage.py collectstatic` should be run for the changes to properly take effect. In general, I deleted quite a bit of javascript code that was unnecessarily cluttering the process.

Also, I added some KPI fields to the `Result` object that were being calculated on the fly before, so `python manage.py migrate` should also be run to apply the new migrations.

Since we are currently accessing [renewables.ninja](renewables.ninja) instead of taking the weather data from the db and processing it with `feedinlib`, this version currently can't reproduce the results of the original offgridplanner as-is. To do the testing for this PR, I exported the PV output calculated in the original `tier-spatial-planning` [dc_output.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21033824/dc_output.csv) and replaced the solar potential in the code by adding the following lines in `solar_potential.py`:

```python
def get_dc_feed_in_sync_db_query(lat, lon, dt_index):
    try:
        weather_df = get_weather_data(lat, lon, dt_index[0], dt_index[-1])
        solar_potential = _get_dc_feed_in(lat, lon, weather_df)
        # I added these lines to test the code with the same PV output
        solar_potential = pd.read_csv("dc_output.csv")["p_mp"][: len(dt_index)]
        solar_potential.index = dt_index
```

Additionally, I imported the consumer list that I exported from the offgridplanner.org example project. 
[offgridplanner_consumers.csv](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21033872/offgridplanner_consumers.6.csv)

With this scenario, I was able to reproduce the results from the offgridplanner example project. I also fixed some small issues I saw that were originally in the offgridplanner, like the average annual demand per consumer actually being calculated as the average hourly consumption. Any remaining inconsistencies in the results should also be older and not newly introduced by this PR.

main()] ``` The `main()]` text was causing a parse error because the closing parenthesis and square bracket combination conflicted with Mermaid's syntax expectations: ``` Parse error on line 10: ... Controller
main()] Sess -----------------------^ Expecting 'SQE', 'DOUBLECIRCLEEND', 'PE', '-)', 'STADIUMEND', 'SUBROUTINEEND', 'PIPE', 'CYLINDEREND', 'DIAMOND_STOP', 'TAGEND', 'TRAPEND', 'INVTRAPEND', 'UNICODE_TEXT', 'TEXT', 'TAGSTART', got 'PS' ``` ## Solution Changed the problematic node definition to use clearer text that maintains the same meaning: ```mermaid MainCtrl[Main Controller

author: amygos
body:
Add --health-cmd and --health-on-failure=kill options to the Podman run
command in the nethcti-ui systemd service. On healthcheck failure,
Podman kills the container, triggering a systemd service restart.

Default Podman healthcheck parameters:
- --health-start-period=0s
- --health-interval=30s
- --health-retries=3

With these defaults, the container is immediately marked as "starting"
at startup. The first healthcheck runs right away and may fail if the
application is not ready. The container remains in the "starting" state
until a healthcheck succeeds or the start period elapses (default 0s).
After three consecutive failed checks (one every 30 seconds), the
container is marked as "unhealthy". This means the application should be
ready within about 1 minute after startup to avoid being marked
unhealthy.

After startup, if the application fails healthchecks, Podman allows up
to three consecutive failures (over 1 minute) before marking the
container as "unhealthy". Then the container is killed and systemd
restarts the service.

Startup example timeline:
0s:   First healthcheck fails (status: starting, failures: 1)
30s:  Second healthcheck fails (status: unhealthy, failures: 2)
60s:  Third healthcheck fails (status: unhealthy, failures: 3)
60s:  The container is killed

After startup example timeline:
0s:   First healthcheck fails (status: healthy, failures: 1)
30s:  Second healthcheck fails (status: healthy, failures: 2)
60s:  Third healthcheck fails (status: unhealthy, failures: 3)
60s:  The container is killed

This ensures the service is restarted automatically if it remains
unhealthy for more than 1 minute.

author: burivuhster
body:
## Summary

This PR upgrades the LangChain packages and improves proxy handling in the @n8n/nodes-langchain package to provide better enterprise proxy support, including NO_PROXY handling.

All LangChain packages have been upgraded to their latest versions, with OpenAI SDK upgraded from v4 to v5.

Breaking change in OpenAI v5: The httpAgent option was removed and replaced with fetchOptions.dispatcher, [requiring the use of undici's dispatcher interface](https://github.com/openai/openai-node?tab=readme-ov-file#configuring-proxies). 

To unify proxy logic with the core nodes (which rely on `getAgentWithProxy` from `requestHelperFunctions`), same `proxy-from-env` approach was used. It allows to respect `NO_PROXY` env variables, but requires `targetUrl` to determine the `proxyUrl`.

As LangChain models only allow providing proxy agent during initialization (and not dynamically) – baseUrls were used instead of targetUrl, which should reasonably cover at least domains specified in `NO_PROXY`.

For some LangChain models it's difficult to know even the domain in advance (e.g. AWS Bedrock Chat). In that case dummy target URL is used, so `NO_PROXY` would not be respected.

### Key Changes

1. Proxy Implementation

- Replaced manual environment variable checking with proxy-from-env package (same approach used in core package)

2. Environment Variable Priority

The new implementation respects the standard proxy environment variable behavior:
- For HTTPS URLs: Uses HTTPS_PROXY or https_proxy
- For HTTP URLs: Uses HTTP_PROXY or http_proxy
- Lowercase variables take precedence over uppercase (following curl/wget conventions) ‼️
- NO_PROXY/no_proxy is respected for excluding hosts from proxy ‼️
- No proxy will be used if target URL is not specified and only HTTP_PROXY environment variable is set ‼️

3. Target URL Handling

- Added optional targetUrl parameter to properly determine which proxy to use (and to handle `NO_PROXY`)
- When target URL is unknown (e.g., AWS Bedrock), uses a dummy URL as fallback
- This ensures proxy support even when the final destination isn't known in advance

### Package Updates

'@langchain/core': 0.3.61
'@langchain/openai': 0.5.16
'@langchain/anthropic': 0.3.23
'@langchain/community': 0.3.47
'langchain': 0.3.29
'openai': 5.8.1  # Major version upgrade from v4

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

- https://linear.app/n8n/issue/AI-1109/tech-debt-upgrade-langchain-including-the-proxy-handling
Closes #16149

   Use `(no-changelog)` otherwise.**
-->
- [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created.
- [x] Tests included. <!--
   A bug is not considered fixed, unless a test is added to prevent it from happening again.
   A feature is not complete without tests.
